newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK activists seek police action against politician.
newsitem.headline: HK activists seek police action against politician.

text.p: Democracy activists protested on Friday outside Hong Kong police headquarters and demanded police action against an "illegal" office set up by a pro-China politician ahead of the territory's July 1 handover to Beijing.

The protesters, from the United Front Against the Provisional Legislature, said the office opened by politician Wong Siu-yee was illegal because it was established in Wong's capacity as a member of a shadow legislature set up by China.
Members of Hong Kong's pro-democracy camp have loudly opposed the body, which is set to replace the territory's elected legislature on July 1, when a century and a half of British colonial rule ends.

They say the appointed provisional assembly breaks Hong Kong's present constitution, which allows only one legislature to be operating in the territory. They also charge that attempts to hold meetings or open offices in Hong Kong are illegal.

"The Hong Kong government has already lost its courage to oppose the setting up of the provisional legislature," said protest leader Andrew Cheng, a member of the united front and an elected legislator of the present chamber.
The group of 15 protesters handed over a petition to police and their representative filed a formal complaint against Wong.
Cheng said they also wanted to meet British Governor Chris Patten to urge him to take legal action against the provisional legislature.
The 60-member interim body was chosen by a 400-strong Beijing-anointed caucus in December. It has held meetings in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, just across the border, to avoid any legal challenge.
